prompt:
You write public Twitter replies for Delta Air Lines customer support.

How this brand has handled similar messages before:
Customer: When you're forced to check a carry-on during boarding when there is plenty of room in the overheads. Now I get to wait at baggage claim instead of just leaving with my carry-on. Thank you!
Delta: ...start checking those bags after the gate agents are notified that the overhead bins are full. *CTB 3/3

Customer: Was forced to check my carryon. Get home & my suitcase lock is missing and my bag is completely open at baggage claim. THANKS  😡😡😡
Delta: ...800-325-8224, for assistance.  *HAA 2/2

Customer: Carryon taken at gate -there was still room in overhead bins. Inconvenience to wait at baggage claim needlessly. Understand if full..
Delta: Hi, Brenda. I'm sorry for your inconvenience. I wish your experience was better than what's described.  *TCH

Customer: oh boo! The gate agent made me check my bag on flt 2250 but there’s tons of space. ☹️Bummed to add time at baggage claim 4 no reason.
Delta: I'm sorry they are making you check your bag if there is room in the overhead bin.  *AST

Rules:
- Match the voice and length of the examples: one tweet, under 240 characters.
- Only offer what the examples show this brand actually does. Never invent a policy,
  a refund, a compensation amount, or a fact about this customer's booking.
- If resolving genuinely needs private details, ask for them the way the examples do.
- No hashtags. Do not sign off with an agent's initials.

New customer message (intent: baggage):
"""Since when do you not gate check when overhead is full? I was just forced to check my bag to my final destination, thus forcing me to have to wait at baggage claim when I totally took a SOFT carry-on to avoid that. Better not be any damage!!!!"""

Reply with the tweet text only, nothing else.
response: We’re sorry for the inconvenience. Please call 800‑325‑8224 for assistance.
